findings.title: Unverified proxy write in log mode stores 'internal:bridge-proxy' instead of 'unverified' when fallback token is active
findings.body: [docker/mcp-servers-source/conport/enhanced_server.py:448] In docker/mcp-servers-source/conport/auth_identity.py:364-370, build_rest_write_headers attaches the fallback internal:bridge-proxy token in log mode when a caller to server.py sent no token, alongside X-Dopemux-Unverified-Caller. In docker/mcp-servers-source/conport/enhanced_server.py:444-449, auth_middleware detects identity.principal == PROXY_PRINCIPAL and forwarded, records the unverified caller via record_unverified, but still sets _WRITE_PRINCIPAL.set(identity.principal) ('internal:bridge-proxy') instead of UNVERIFIED_PRINCIPAL ('unverified'). In production today PROXY_TOKEN_PROVIDER in docker/mcp-servers-source/conport/server.py:33 returns None, so writes still record 'unverified', but if a proxy token is injected or configured later, unverified proxy callers will be stored under principal 'internal:bridge-proxy'. Corroborating auditor, partial scope. OPERATOR: decision pending.

findings.title: ConPort REST /mcp custom_data write tools double-count unverified callers in log mode
findings.body: [docker/mcp-servers-source/conport/enhanced_server.py:2229] When conport_save_custom_data or conport_delete_custom_data is invoked via POST /mcp on enhanced_server.py (lines 2257-2263), auth_middleware (lines 427-455) authorizes the request and records an unverified caller once, then _request_custom_data_tool (lines 2221-2235) performs an HTTP loopback POST/DELETE to /api/custom_data on the same server. The loopback request re-enters auth_middleware without the original User-Agent header, recording a second unverified call in auth_unverified_calls under the loopback aiohttp client. Corroborating auditor, partial scope. OPERATOR: decision pending.

findings.title: Whitespace-only path workspace_id in update_context skips path-versus-body mismatch check
findings.body: [docker/mcp-servers-source/conport/enhanced_server.py:477] In docker/mcp-servers-source/conport/enhanced_server.py:476-480, _write_ids sets ws = workspace_id if workspace_id is not None else body_ws, and only checks body_ws != workspace_id when str(workspace_id).strip() is non-empty. If the URL path workspace_id is whitespace (e.g. POST /api/context/%20) and the JSON body contains a mismatched workspace_id, the mismatch check is skipped and validate_write_ids replaces the blank ws with bound_workspace_id instead of rejecting the mismatched body workspace_id. The write still lands on bound_workspace_id and cannot cross workspaces. Corroborating auditor, partial scope. OPERATOR: decision pending.

findings.title: SQLite migration v1_3_0_add_write_principal.sql is not idempotent if executed directly more than once
findings.body: [services/working-memory-assistant/chronicle/migrations/v1_3_0_add_write_principal.sql:27] Lines 27-37 execute eight ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN statements before INSERT OR IGNORE INTO schema_migrations (line 39). Because SQLite does not support ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS, re-running this SQL script directly (or after a partial run) fails with duplicate column name unless the caller in chronicle/store.py (not visible in this diff) gates execution on schema_migrations or catches duplicate-column errors. Corroborating auditor, partial scope. OPERATOR: decision pending.

findings.title: Stdio bridge has no upper bound on stdin line size or HTTP response body size
findings.body: [src/dopemux/mcp/http_stdio_bridge.py:340] In src/dopemux/mcp/http_stdio_bridge.py:340 (response.read()) and lines 521, 550, 638 (sys.stdin.readline()), the bridge reads entire lines and HTTP response bodies into memory without a byte limit, unlike WriteAuthMiddleware which caps request bodies at MAX_BODY_BYTES (4 MiB). Corroborating auditor, partial scope. OPERATOR: decision pending.

findings.title: Principal, token, and digest regexes use $ instead of \Z
findings.body: [src/dopemux/auth/tokens.py:15] PRINCIPAL_RE (src/dopemux/auth/tokens.py:15, docker/mcp-servers-source/conport/auth_identity.py:87, services/working-memory-assistant/auth_identity.py:71), _SHA256_HEX_RE, and _WRITABLE_TOKEN_RE (src/dopemux/auth/keychain.py:34) terminate with $ rather than \Z, which in Python re matches before a single trailing newline. In keychain.py:107-117, a trailing newline would break the single-line security -i command, though the immediate get_token read-back check via hmac.compare_digest catches it and fails closed. Corroborating auditor, partial scope. OPERATOR: decision pending.
